title: ophrys oestrifera subsp. hygrophila
intro: Ophrys oestrifera subsp. hygrophila, commonly known as the Marsh Fly Orchid, is a type of orchid that belongs to the Ophrys genus. The Marsh Fly Orchid is known for its unique and delicate appearance, with flowers that resemble female flies, which in turn attract male flies for pollination. The plant is valued for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help to soothe digestive issues and protect against cell damage. The bioactive constituents of the Marsh Fly Orchid include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, such as antispasmodic and anti-inflammatory effects.
